rules.title: Source of income discrimination ban (FEHA)
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) - source of income
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to you or treat you differently because of how you pay rent, including Section 8 vouchers or other rental assistance.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden negarse a alquilarle ni tratarlo de manera diferente por la forma en que paga el alquiler, incluidos los vales de la Sección 8 u otra ayuda para el alquiler.
rules.coverage_text: Most housing providers and housing-related services in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
rules.quote: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).

rules.title: Limits on criminal history screening (FEHA)
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) - criminal history
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot ban everyone with a record. A denial must be based on a conviction directly related to being a good tenant.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios pueden revisar antecedentes penales, pero no pueden considerar arrestos sin condena, registros sellados o borrados, ni registros juveniles, y no pueden rechazar a todas las personas con antecedentes. Un rechazo debe basarse en una condena directamente relacionada con ser un buen inquilino.
rules.coverage_text: Most housing providers and housing-related services in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
rules.quote: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
